title: Orsen and the Compass
premise: In 1911, Hazel Ashgrove, daughter of a pearl diver and indentured to the Meridian Trading Company, has learned that history is something that happens to other people — until a sealed letter, hidden in her late father's diving chest, names her family as keepers of evidence against the company's founder. The letter proves Meridian sank a rival fleet and drowned thirty divers to seize the pearl beds, and three checkpoints between Hazel's island home and the colonial magistrate stand between truth and silence. Guided by her father's old compass, which points not north but toward what was lost, Hazel smuggles the evidence through storm, betrayal, and the company's hunters, discovering that survival itself can be an inheritance of guilt. At the final checkpoint she must choose between burning the letter to save her mother's freedom or delivering it and condemning them both to the company's wrath — and in the end she does neither, reading it aloud to the assembled divers, making the memory theirs.
about_author: Rafael Fairweather is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trading-company ledgers from the South Sea pearling era. They write historical fiction about the people those ledgers reduced to line items.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Hazel dives the shallows for company pearls while her mother mends nets, establishing their indenture to Meridian and Hazel's belief that big events happen elsewhere. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: quiet resignation masking a fierce, unadmitted curiosity.

chapters.title: A Chest That Should Have Stayed Shut
chapters.summary: Clearing her drowned father's belongings for the company's inventory clerk, Hazel finds a sealed letter wedged beneath a brass compass. The wax bears a magistrate's crest. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: dread blooming where grief had settled.

chapters.title: What the Letter Says
chapters.summary: Unable to read the dense legal hand alone, Hazel brings the letter to Old Sefa, a retired diver who once served the rival fleet. He goes pale: it names witnesses to the sinking of the Lorelei fleet — including Hazel's father. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of her small world.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Sefa explains the route to the colonial magistrate: the ferry at Salt Quay, the customs house at Grey Reach, and the company fort at Tern Gate. Each is watched by Meridian men. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: grim resolve; an old man choosing to finish a debt.

chapters.title: The Compass That Lies
chapters.summary: Hazel discovers her father's compass needle swings toward the sunken Lorelei wreck, not north. Diving it, she finds a second document — the fleet's manifest proving the sabotage. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear of what her father carried.

chapters.title: Company Men at the Door
chapters.summary: An auditor arrives to finalize the Ashgrove indenture and searches the house. Hazel hides the letter inside a net float; her mother lies smoothly for the first time in her life. POV: Mother (Maren). Emotional beat: maternal terror sharpening into complicity.

chapters.title: Indentured No Longer
chapters.summary: Hazel buys out her contract with pearls from the wreck, freeing herself — and binding herself to the mission. Sefa warns that freed divers who talk disappear. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: the intoxicating, frightening taste of choice.

chapters.title: Salt Quay
chapters.summary: First checkpoint: Hazel sews the letter into her coat lining and boards the ferry among fishwives. A Meridian spotter boards behind her. She passes inspection by pretending deafness. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: white-knuckle stillness.

chapters.title: The Spotter's Name
chapters.summary: On the crossing, Hazel recognizes the spotter: Tam Voss, a boy from her village now on company pay. He half-recognizes her too. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: his loyalty wavering between wage and conscience.

chapters.title: Grey Reach Customs House
chapters.summary: Second checkpoint: a thorough search. Maren, traveling separately as decoy, is detained when contraband pearls are planted in her bag. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered without being asked.

chapters.title: The Bargain at Grey Reach
chapters.summary: Hazel must choose: surrender the letter to free her mother, or push on. She trades the wreck's loose pearls instead — everything but the documents — buying Maren's release and their last funds. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: grief for the inheritance she keeps spending down.

chapters.title: Tam Catches Up
chapters.summary: Tam confronts Hazel on the marsh road, orders in hand to retrieve 'stolen company property.' She tells him the truth about the Lorelei. He lets her pass — and reports a false sighting. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: the cost of a first betrayal of one's employers.

chapters.title: The Fort at Tern Gate
chapters.summary: They scout the third checkpoint: the only road to the magistrate runs through the fort's gate, and Sefa's contact there has vanished. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: hope thinning to a thread.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: Waiting in a smuggler's loft, Sefa confesses he survived the Lorelei sinking by clinging to wreckage while others drowned — and stayed silent for forty years. The letter's witnesses were paid to forget. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: shame transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Festival Cover
chapters.summary: A lantern festival will flood the fort road with crowds. Hazel plans to walk through openly, letter hidden in a festival lantern, betting that audacity beats stealth. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: fear converted into defiance.

chapters.title: Tern Gate Burns Its Lanterns
chapters.summary: At the gate, guards confiscate all lanterns — including hers. In the scramble, Hazel slips the letter to Maren, who walks through as a grieving widow delivering memorial papers. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: mother and daughter reversing roles; the keeper becomes the carrier.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Magistrate's Steps
chapters.summary: On the magistrate's steps, Tam appears — ordered to finish the job, having been discovered in his false report. Instead he testifies aloud, naming what Meridian did to his own family. Guards seize him. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: redemption purchased at full price.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Inside, the magistrate hesitates — Meridian's money reaches high. Hazel makes her choice: neither burn nor file the letter, but read it aloud from the steps to the gathered divers and fishwives, dozens of voices taking up the words. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: private evidence becoming public memory.

chapters.title: The Company Answers
chapters.summary: Meridian's men move to disperse the crowd; Sefa stands on the steps and begins reciting the names of the drowned. One by one, divers kneel and speak names of their own until the square cannot be cleared. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: mourning as resistance.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Forced by public record and Tam's sworn testimony, the magistrate opens an inquiry; Meridian's charter is suspended pending trial. It is not full justice — the founder flees abroad — but the lie is dead. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: victory with ash in its mouth.

chapters.title: The Compass Rests
chapters.summary: Hazel dives the Lorelei one last time and leaves the compass on the wreck, its needle finally still. Her indenture contract burns in the kitchen stove. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: release; laying down inherited weight.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: A year later, Hazel teaches village children to read using the transcript of the reading; Maren dives again for herself, not the company. History, Hazel understands now, happens to everyone — the question is who remembers it. POV: Hazel. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed as story rather than burden.
